title: Release RepoPact 3.0.1 and Reconcile Stable Source/Artifact Identity

preflight.note: Recorded before 3.0.1 release implementation begins. Triggered by a clean Windows/PyPI reproduction proving that public repopact==3.0.0 and current main both advertise 3.0.0 while loading different stable runtime code: the public wheel lacks the post-release worktree exclusion present on main.

acceptance_criteria.text: A durable release-gap evidence record compares the v3.0.0 tag, the public PyPI repopact==3.0.0 wheel, and the exact pre-3.0.1 main commit. It records commit/tag/package identity, the complete executable/package delta (not only documentation), and reproduces in an isolated environment that the public 3.0.0 wheel lacks the stable worktree exclusion while main contains it.

An accepted release decision defines 3.0.1 as a backwards-compatible corrective release for stable post-v3.0.0 changes already accepted on main. The decision explicitly enumerates what runtime/package changes ship and confirms that proposed WI042, WI043, and WI044 implementation work is not pulled into 3.0.1 merely because those planning records exist on main.

The 3.0.1 release tree consistently identifies the release across VERSION, conformance suite identity, README/current-release guidance, release decision/narrative, and any other governed release surfaces required by existing RepoPact validation; generated artifacts are regenerated rather than hand-maintained.

The work formally reconciles stable source identity with published artifact identity. It evaluates the existing decision 0026 RELEASE_LABEL mechanism, immediate next-development-version transitions, package-metadata derivation, and release/tag-aware validation (or justified equivalents), then records one durable rule: after a stable version is published/tagged, subsequent package/runtime-affecting source state on main must not remain indistinguishable from that published artifact solely because VERSION is unchanged.

The chosen source/artifact identity rule is implemented at the narrowest effective layer and has regression/conformance coverage. Positive coverage preserves an exact clean release tree; negative coverage demonstrates that a post-release package/runtime change cannot silently present the same governed release identity as the already-published stable artifact. Existing adopter VERSION equality semantics are not weakened accidentally.

From the exact clean 3.0.1 release commit, `repopact release-build` produces sdist and wheel twice from independent exports with fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and byte-identical hashes, while all existing package-boundary checks remain satisfied (single repopact import root, required packaged schemas/templates, no deprecated flat modules or data-files).

The exact locally validated 3.0.1 wheel installs into a clean Windows virtual environment outside the source checkout and proves the stable post-3.0.0 behavior is actually packaged, including `"worktrees" in repopact.repo_model.IGNORED_PARTS` evaluating True. Installed CLI init/adopt/validate smoke behavior and package-resource access also remain green.

Before publication, the exact release tree passes RepoPact governance validation, the full unit suite, all conformance cases, dashboard/spec regeneration checks, twine metadata validation, and the frozen-surface backstop. Any skipped test or unavailable remote check is disclosed rather than counted as passing.

The release commit and annotated v3.0.1 tag are pushed and resolve to the same exact commit. The exact validated wheel and sdist are published to PyPI; public metadata reports 3.0.1; a no-cache download's SHA-256 matches the locally validated artifact; and a clean public-wheel install outside the checkout proves the worktree exclusion and supported CLI behavior from site-packages.

The selected identity mechanism defines and tests the post-publication transition for future main development so RepoPact cannot repeat the observed state where an already-published stable artifact and materially newer package/runtime source both claim an indistinguishable stable identity. The rule must distinguish an unchanged release commit from later runtime-affecting development rather than declaring the release tag itself invalid.

Package publication remains distinct from adopter-fleet migration and remote-CI restoration. WI037 continues to own downstream adoption/package-boundary reconciliation and WI032 continues to own remote enforcement; WI045 closeout must not claim either obligation complete merely because 3.0.1 is public.
